named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Ukrainian journal article arguing that integrating smart robots into society needs an interdisciplinary approach. It analyses three approaches to robot rights: the 'electronic person' concept, moral rights of robots, and the social-relational approach, which it treats as human-centred. It calls for theoretical and empirical methodology to ground robots' rights and obligations.
annotation.title_clean: Філософсько-правові питання інтеграції розумних роботів у суспільство
annotation.title_en: Philosophical and legal issues of integration of smart robots into society
key_provisions_or_claims: Robot integration requires an interdisciplinary approach.
Three approaches to robot rights: electronic person, moral rights, social-relational.
Social-relational approach is regarded as human-centred.
EU 2016-2017 proposals floated 'electronic person' status for advanced autonomous robots; most countries, including the US, take a wait-and-see stance.
A methodology for theoretical and empirical grounding of robots' rights and obligations is needed.
